discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitaet Muenchen

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller laid the conceptual foundations for controlling quantum matter atom by atom: their 1995 proposal for quantum logic with trapped ions, and their 1998 prediction (with Jaksch and co-workers) that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable interactions, turned Feynman's vision of quantum simulation into a concrete programme. Bloch's 2002 observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition confirmed this prediction and started a field. His later work on single-site resolved imaging, many-body localization and synthetic gauge fields made optical lattices a precision tool for strongly correlated physics. Together, their work created a new way of doing condensed-matter physics with engineered, fully controllable quantum systems. The approach has since spread to Rydberg arrays, ions and superconducting circuits, and it now underpins today's efforts toward scalable quantum simulators and fault-tolerant quantum computers.
